rationale: This is a very small program (1266 text bytes, 32 functions, largest only 139 bytes) that spends its time in tight array-stepping loops (testA/testB/testC, stepA), so the table favors cheap, correctness-safe passes applied broadly: SUB gets the highest SecurityGain/DiversityGain weights because instruction substitution adds strong static-analysis friction at near-zero runtime and size cost on integer-heavy code; SPLIT and IBR are similarly low-cost diversifiers applied widely; and IGV is weighted moderately because the workload is array/global-state-centric, making global data obfuscation well-matched at minimal overhead. FLA is retained with moderate weights to flatten the main test drivers for real resistance, but its SizeCost/CorrectnessRisk weights are elevated relative to SUB/SPLIT so it is applied selectively rather than to every small function. BCF is deliberately down-weighted (high SizeCost 0.7, RuntimeCost 0.6) because bogus-control-flow bloat would be disproportionate on 67-139 byte functions and would penalize the hot stepping loops, keeping total size and runtime growth acceptable while the cheaper passes carry the bulk of the hardening. ICALL keeps a modest security weight with the highest CorrectnessRisk (0.3) of the set, so indirect-call transformation is applied conservatively; all seven passes remain enabled, with cost dimensions acting as the brake on where the expensive passes land.
